reason: The engine owns durable next-turn input and all execution admission. The desktop projects engine rows into composer snapshots and imports its legacy SQLite rows and receipts exactly once. Metadata mutations use the named thread/queue facade. Portable native attachment bytes are saved before enqueue completes, so delivery survives removal of the original temporary file. One in-memory host lock may coordinate delivery preparation, while atomic thread/queue/start owns admission and removal. A transport timeout never authorizes a local fallback or a second model submission. A successful admission is separate from application of a steer. Host reads omit native input bytes and retain complete presentation metadata plus native-input fingerprint and row-version fences. A changed row at final reserve is a definite CAS refusal, including Stop. External text reads use the same revision and absolute offset. Atomic clear retires rows without creating Undo proof and preserves permanent replay identities. A confirmed addition remains accepted when its later snapshot read fails, preventing duplicate recovery input.
